summary: Independent verification of the WAITLIST MANAGEMENT + CONSENT CAPTURE phase. Backend: new pytest suite /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (13 tests, 13 passed) covering seeded waitlist shape/enrichment, add-with/without-consent, server-side consentGivenAt, duplicate-phone 409, validation 400s, 404s, double-consent 409, remove, broadcast consent gate (non-consented skipped, consented gets exactly 1, removed gets 0), 0000 failure-isolation hook, no money tokens in message bodies, and the seeded 4-consented/2-skipped/3-sent/1-failed regression. Frontend: full Playwright E2E on the public preview URL — all 9 requested scenarios PASSED (panel counts '4 consented'/'2 without consent', honest NO CONSENT badges, unchecked-by-default checkbox, 'Add without consent' label, zero messages before consent, exact consent copy match on inline panel and in stored consentText, server ISO timestamp, duplicate-phone error with unchanged counts, two-step remove with cancel path, zero messages after removal, copy-safety scan clean, broadcast stats 4/2/3/1 after re-seed). DB re-seeded (seed.py --reset) at the end so demo slots are fresh.

minor.issue: remove_entry() deletes only the WaitlistEntry and leaves the orphan Patient doc, while the duplicate check in add_patient_with_consent() queries the patients collection. Result: a removed patient can NEVER be re-added with the same phone — POST returns 409 'A patient with this phone number is already on this clinic's waitlist' even though they are not on the waitlist (reproduced: removed Priya +919876543210, re-add -> 409 while waitlist has 6 rows). Fix: check waitlist_entries (join on phone) for the duplicate, or reuse/soft-clean the orphan patient.

issues: Cosmetic/data-only: seeded rows display the OLD consent copy ('I consent to receive WhatsApp notifications about available last-minute dental appointment slots from Smile Dental, Indiranagar.') while consent.js generates the new copy. Historic records showing verbatim stored text is correct behaviour, but the demo looks inconsistent — consider aligning seed.py text with lib/consent.js.

action_items: Fix duplicate-phone check so a removed waitlist patient can be re-added (currently permanent 409 due to orphan Patient doc)
Optional: align seed.py consent text with lib/consent.js copy for demo consistency
critical_code_review_comments: Broadcast query in routes/clinics.py open_slot_and_broadcast is unchanged ({consentGivenAt: {$ne: None}}) — verified by behaviour: non-consented/removed patients get zero sent_messages and skippedNonConsented is computed as total - consented.
consentGivenAt is set exclusively in waitlist_service._now_iso() — captured browser POST bodies contain no timestamp field (verified via request interception on both add and record-consent calls).
list_enriched does N+1 patient lookups per row (fine at demo scale; consider $lookup if the waitlist grows).
All waitlist endpoints project {_id: 0} / strip _id — no ObjectId leakage observed.
seed_data_creation: Backend tests create an isolated 'TEST_Waitlist Clinic' with TEST_ patients and their own slots (so seeded demo slots are not consumed). UI test added/consented/removed 'Priya Menon' (+919876543210) on the seeded clinic. Final state: `python /app/backend/seed.py --reset` was re-run, so seeded clinic is clean (4 consented + 2 non-consented, slot_today_1000/1130/1630 scheduled). TEST_ clinic data remains in DB but is isolated.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Waitlist phase fully verified end-to-end. Broadcasting consumes scheduled slots (slot_today_1000/1130/1630) — re-run `python /app/backend/seed.py --reset` before repeating UI flows. Backend regression suite: `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/backend_test.py -v` (creates its own clinic/slots, safe to re-run repeatedly). Only open defect: orphan Patient doc after waitlist removal blocks re-adding the same phone.
rca_of_the_issue: Re-add 409 RCA: services/waitlist_service.remove_entry only deletes from waitlist_entries; add_patient_with_consent's duplicate guard queries patients by (clinicId, phone), so the surviving patient record permanently blocks re-registration and the 409 message is factually wrong.
